summary: Elective urology admission of a man with known bilateral staghorn renal calculi and bilateral percutaneous nephrostomy tubes for definitive stone treatment. He underwent difficult right percutaneous nephrolithotomy for stone >2 cm with antegrade nephrostogram, antegrade ureteroscopy, antegrade ureteral stent placement and removal of the right nephrostomy tube, with residual stone burden requiring interval ureteroscopy. Post-operative course was uncomplicated (POD1 discharge); labs show stable chronic renal impairment (Cr 2.1 → 2.5) and normocytic/macrocytic anemia (Hgb 9.4).
most_likely: Staghorn calculus of right kidney requiring percutaneous nephrolithotomy

differential.diagnosis: Bilateral staghorn calculi of kidney (right renal calculus treated this stay)
supporting_evidence: Right PCNL for stone greater than 2 cm performed
differential.reasoning: Admission was explicitly for planned stone removal; the renal calculus is the disease driving the entire stay and all procedures.

differential.diagnosis: Chronic kidney disease, stage 4, from long-standing obstructive nephropathy
supporting_evidence: Creatinine 2.1–2.5 mg/dL persistently over three admissions
Prior ICD N18.9; bilateral atrophic thin renal parenchyma on prior imaging
opposing_evidence: Exact stage/eGFR not reported this stay
differential.reasoning: Stable elevated creatinine with prior documented renal atrophy supports chronic kidney disease as a major active comorbidity affecting perioperative care.

differential.diagnosis: Hydronephrosis with renal and ureteral calculous obstruction (obstructive uropathy)
supporting_evidence: Prior ICD N13.2 with bilateral PCN tubes for obstructive uropathy
Antegrade nephrostogram and ureteral stent placed this stay
opposing_evidence: Current note does not restate active hydronephrosis
differential.reasoning: Chronic calculous obstruction is the documented indication for the nephrostomy/stent pathway and remains a plausible coded principal or secondary condition.

supporting_evidence: Prior ICD D63.1 anemia in CKD; ferritin 257, TSAT 22%
opposing_evidence: Macrocytosis (MCV 104) not typical of pure CKD anemia
differential.reasoning: Persistent anemia paralleling CKD, though rising MCV and recent surgery raise alternative contributions.

supporting_evidence: PMH hypertension documented; prior ICD I12.9
opposing_evidence: No antihypertensive medications on admission; vitals stable (AVSS)
differential.reasoning: Longstanding hypertension coexisting with CKD is a codable chronic comorbidity, though untreated and quiescent this stay.

differential.diagnosis: Presence of ureteral stent and nephrostomy tube status with residual stone burden
supporting_evidence: Right antegrade ureteral stent placed; right nephrostomy tube removed
Residual stone requiring interval right ureteroscopy
opposing_evidence: Device/status codes are not principal diagnoses
differential.reasoning: Status and residual disease are documented and codable as secondary items driving planned follow-up procedures.

differential.diagnosis: Hemiplegia following prior nontraumatic intracerebral hemorrhage, left nondominant side
supporting_evidence: PMH hemorrhagic CVA with residual left upper extremity weakness
opposing_evidence: No current neurologic deficit described in exam
differential.reasoning: Chronic sequela consistently coded in prior stays; relevant to mobility/perioperative care though not active now.

differential.diagnosis: Acute kidney injury superimposed on chronic kidney disease, post-procedural
opposing_evidence: Small change within prior baseline range 2.1–2.3
differential.reasoning: Modest post-operative creatinine rise could represent transient AKI but may simply be baseline CKD fluctuation.

supporting_evidence: Prior admission with Serratia UTI and pyonephrosis coding
opposing_evidence: Urine culture: mixed flora consistent with contamination
differential.reasoning: Historically relevant but current cultures and inflammatory markers argue against active infection this stay.

rule_outs.why: Exam notes no hematoma at PCN site; Hgb stable 9.8 → 9.4 without transfusion.
Afebrile, normal WBC, contaminated urine culture, discharged POD1.
Extremities without edema and no calf tenderness on exam.

uncertain_areas: Whether an obstructing/hydronephrotic component was documented intraoperatively (would support N13.2 as principal over N20.0)
Exact CKD stage/eGFR to code stage 4 vs unspecified
Whether post-op creatinine rise was formally called AKI on CKD
Stone composition and whether left kidney stone treatment was addressed this stay
